summary: SSO assertion / session TTL mismatch prevents access to Kubernetes dashboard behind auth-proxy
description:
Issue summary: Multiple internal users could not access the Kubernetes dashboard via the internal Console. Requests returned a 401/403 shortly after login and sessions were being dropped intermittently.

Impact: Prevented engineers from using the k8s dashboard for cluster troubleshooting for ~90 minutes across the us-west prod environment. Approximately 6 oncall and platform engineers affected.

Environment: prod-us-west, console behind auth-proxy v3.7.2, Okta SSO (OIDC) session TTL configured at 8h, auth-proxy session cache TTL set to 5m.

Observed behavior: After completing Okta SSO flow and being redirected back to the Console, users could click into the Kubernetes dashboard, but were immediately redirected to the login screen or saw 403s. Session cookies (console_session) persisted in the browser, but the auth-proxy returned 401 on the dashboard route.

Expected behavior: Successful single-sign-on into Console should grant uninterrupted access to k8s dashboard for the duration of Console session (8h) or until user logs out.

Attachments: auth-proxy logs, sample okta token claim dump, screenshots of 403 page.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Sign in to Console via Okta SSO (OIDC) in prod-us-west.
2) Complete redirect back to Console landing page.
3) From the Console navigation open 'Kubernetes > Dashboard'.
4) Observe immediate redirect to /login or a 403 error, despite console_session cookie present.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:18 - Ethan Morales: Reported that dashboard link throws 403 for multiple users after SSO. Included browser devtools HAR and console_session cookie header.
2026-03-12 09:25 - Support Triage (Ana Lopez): Acknowledged. Assigned to Priya. Noted spike in 403s from auth-proxy logs starting at 09:05 UTC.

2026-03-12 09:40 - Priya Nair: Investigating logs. auth-proxy shows 'session not found' for valid cookie values; Okta token exchange returns 200 and id_token expiry (exp) is 8h out. Suspect cache eviction mismatch between OIDC session refresh logic and auth-proxy authorization cache.
2026-03-12 10:05 - Platform Eng (Marcus Li): Noted we recently rolled auth-proxy change that shortened internal cache TTL to 5m to reduce memory. Linking PR #842 which landed this morning.

2026-03-12 11:10 - Priya Nair: Applied temporary mitigation: rolled back auth-proxy cache TTL to 15m via a staged config change on prod-us-west for the dashboard route. Observing reduction in failures. Will continue validation.
2026-03-14 08:03 - Priya Nair: Root cause confirmed and permanent fix merged. Closing after monitoring period.
investigation_notes: auth-proxy logs (prod-us-west) show repeated 'auth cache miss' entries at 09:05-09:45 UTC correlating with user timestamps.
Okta token dumps show exp claim consistent with 8h TTL; tokens are still valid when auth-proxy returns 401 for the same request.
Heap and descriptor metrics on auth-proxy host indicate recent memory pressure; the cache eviction policy (LRU) was trimming entries aggressively after the recent config change.

Reproduced locally by setting auth-proxy cache TTL=5m and issuing an OIDC login; after ~2 minutes subsequent requests to protected subroutes fail despite valid cookies because the proxy requires a cached session-to-principal mapping for the dashboard path.

Hypothesis: Short TTL for auth-proxy session mapping caused legitimate sessions to be evicted before the Console's session cookie lifetime. The dashboard path performs an additional auth check (impersonation header present) that requires the mapping to be in cache; eviction leads to 401/403.
Temporary mitigation: increased cache TTL to 15m in prod-us-west for auth-proxy and rebalanced memory limits on proxy hosts to avoid thrashing.

Permanent fix: updated auth-proxy to rehydrate session mapping from Okta on cache miss (fall back to token validation) and added adaptive TTL logic. PRs: auth-proxy#842 (revert aggressive TTL) and auth-proxy#847 (rehydration fallback) linked above.
resolution:
Root cause: auth-proxy session cache TTL was reduced in a recent deploy, causing valid Okta sessions to lose their in-memory mapping and leading to immediate 401/403 when hitting the k8s dashboard route (which performs extra permission lookup). Remediation: rolled back the aggressive TTL change to 15m as an interim measure, increased proxy memory limits, and merged a permanent fix that rehydrates session mappings from Okta on cache miss and implements adaptive TTL based on route sensitivity.

Follow-up actions:
- Postmortem scheduled (owner: Priya Nair) and will include an action to add e2e test covering auth-proxy cache miss behavior for dashboard flows.
- Deploy auth-proxy#847 to all regions and monitor for 48 hours.
- Update runbook: add a step for checking 'auth cache miss' and guidance for safe TTL values.
- Notify Platform and SRE teams; communicate change to oncall rotation.

Status: Resolved and monitored for 48h with no recurrence in prod-us-west as of 2026-03-14.
